articles.text: WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Nín hǎo! Huānyíng nín lái wǒmen xuéyuàn cānguān.
UYGUR STUDENT: Hello! Welcome to the Institute.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Nǐde Hànyǔ hěn hǎo ma, shi zài Běijīng xuéde ma?
AMERICAN: Your Chinese is very good! Did you learn it in Běijīng?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Zhǔyào shi zài Běijīng xuéde, kěshi bú shi zài Běijīng kāishǐ xuéde.
UYGUR STUDENT: Mainly, but I wasn't in Běijīng when I started learning it.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Ō, zài Xīnjiāng Wéiwúěr Zìzhìqūde xuéxiàoli yě jiāo Hànyǔ, shì bu shì?
AMERICAN: Oh. They teach Chinese in schools in the Xīnjiāng Uygur Autonomous Region, do they?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Zài zìzhìqūde zhōng-xiǎoxuéli chúle Hànzú xuéxiào yǐwài dōu jiāo shǎoshù mínzú wénzì, tèbié shi Wéiwúěr wénzì.
UYGUR STUDENT: Except for the Han nationality schools, secondary and primary schools in the autonomous region teach the minority nationality languages, especially the Uygur language.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Wéiwúěr wénzì hé Zhōngdōngde wénzì yǒu shénme guānxi ma?
AMERICAN: Is the Uygur language related to the languages of the Middle East?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Yǒu, Wéiwúěryǔ hé Tǔěrqíyǔ bǐjiào jìn, lǎo Wéiwúěrwén jīběnshang shi Ālābówén, xīn wénzì yòngde shi Lādīng zìmǔ.
UYGUR STUDENT: Yes. Uygur is rather close to Turkish. The old Uygur writing system was basically an Arabic writing system. The new writing system uses the Roman alphabet.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Nàme xiàng "Gòngchǎndǎng," "Shèhuìzhǔyì" zhèixiē zì zěnme bàn ne?
AMERICAN: Well, how do they handle words like "the Communist Party" and "socialism"?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Zhèixiē zìde fāyīn duōbàn xiàng Hànyǔ, huòzhě xiàng Éyǔ.
UYGUR STUDENT: The pronunciation of words like that is mostly like Chinese, or like Russian.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Duìbuqǐ, Wéiwúěr rén dǒng Hànyǔde duō ne, háishi dǒng Éyǔde duō ne?
AMERICAN: I'm sorry: Do more Uygurs understand Chinese or Russian?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Yìbānde lái shuō, hái shi dǒng Éwénde rén duō.
UYGUR STUDENT: Generally speaking, there are still more who understand Russian.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Duì le--nǐ gāngcái bú shi shuō nǐde Hànyǔ bú shi zài Běijīng kāishǐ xuéde ma?
AMERICAN: Oh--you just said that you didn't begin studying Chinese in Běijīng, right?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Wǒmen lái Běijīng niàn dàxuéde shǎoshù mínzú xuéshēng dōu kěyi zài zìzhìqūde Hànzú xuéxiàoli xiān xué yìnián Hànyǔ. Zài xué Hànyǔ yǐqián, wǒ lián yíge Hànzì dōu bù zhīdao.

UYGUR STUDENT: All of us minority students who come to Běijīng to attend college can take a year of Chinese language beforehand in a Han nationality school in the autonomous region. Before I started studying Chinese, I didn't even know one Chinese character.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Hànyǔ shi hěn fùzáde, xuéqilai dàgài hěn nán.
AMERICAN: Chinese is very complicated. It must be very hard to study.
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Bù juéde zěnme tài nán, xuéle yìnián yǐhòu wǒmen hé nàrde Hànzú gōngren, gànbu, yòng Hànyǔ tǎolùn wèntí, jiāoliú sīxiǎng dōu méiyou shénme wèntí le.
UYGUR STUDENT: I don't find it terribly difficult. After one year, we didn't have any problem having discussions and communicating ideas in Chinese with the Chinese workers and cadres there.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Tz! Nà zhēn bú cuò. Duì le--wǒ hái yǒu zuìhòu yíge xiǎo wèntí. Nǐmen xìn jiào ma?
AMERICAN: Gee, that's really great. Oh yes--I have one last small question. Do you profess a religion?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Wǒmende fùmǔ, zǔfùmǔ dōu xiāngxìn Yīsīlánjiào.
UYGUR STUDENT: Our parents and grandparents believe in Islam.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Nǐmen zìjǐ ne?
AMERICAN: What about you yourselves?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Wǒmen zìjǐ me, yǒude xìn, yǒude bú tài xìn, wǒ hái shi xiāngxìnde.
UYGUR STUDENT: We ourselves...well, some of us believe, and some of us don't really believe. I still believe.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Zài Běijīng yě kěyi zuò lǐbài ma?
AMERICAN: Can you worship in Běijīng?
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Kěyi. Zhèr yǒu hěn dàde qīngzhēnsì, wǒ měige xīngqī dōu qù.
UYGUR STUDENT: Yes. There's a big mosque here. I go every week.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Tài xièxie nǐ le, gěi wǒ jièshàole zhème duō yǒu yìside qíngkuàng.
AMERICAN: Thank you so much for telling me about so many interesting things.
WÉIWÚĚR XUÉSHENG: Hěn gāoxìng nín lái cānguān. Zàijiàn.
UYGUR STUDENT: It was nice to have you here. Good-bye.
MĚIGUÓ RÉN: Zàijiàn.
AMERICAN: Good-bye.
